text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementHealthHow Your Body Clock Affects Your Mental Health and Ways to Keep It in SyncOur internal body clock helps regulate sleep, alertness and mood, following a roughly 24-hour cycle influenced by light and darknessSCBy Sarah Chellappa11:00 AM CST on November 5, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleEver wondered why a bad night’s sleep can leave you irritable, anxious or sad? Poor sleep affects our emotions, but its timing also plays a role.Our circadian rhythms are nearly 24-hour cycles that regulate alertness, hormones, body temperature and digestion.Deep inside the brain, a cluster of nerve cells called the suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) acts as the body’s master clock. It uses light signals from the eyes to coordinate clocks in other organs, including the brain, liver, heart and gut.Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
